seo.title: Pairing with Caribbean Cuisine · Kibay at Ocoa Bay
seo.description: Kibay pairs with ceviche, fresh seafood, soft cheeses, and farm-to-table cooking. Try the Casa Club menu at Ocoa Bay, at a table with a view over the valley.

hero.eyebrow: Reason #3 · A Way to Enjoy Kibay
hero.title: The table, the wine, the Caribbean
hero.lead: Ceviche, seafood, fresh cheese, farm-to-table cooking. Kibay isn't a side note — it's part of the plate.
hero.imageAlt: Caribbean dish paired with a glass of Kibay sparkling at Casa Club

story.heading: Caribbean wine, Caribbean food, same origin
story.p1: Some wines were made for a cuisine they've never met. Kibay wasn't. The sparkling of mango and passion fruit grew on the same property where the ingredients on the Casa Club table are harvested — the same sun, the same soil, the same Atlantic wind. That's why it converses with the food instead of competing with it.
story.p2: Try it with a fresh ceviche: the acidity of the Kibay clears the palate and the citrus in the dish stays bright. With a soft goat cheese, the fruit of the wine rounds out and turns almost creamy. With a baked mahi-mahi, the tropical aromatics sit beside the fish like family.
story.p3: The menu shifts with the season because the property shifts with the season. That's part of the deal. Book a table, let the kitchen team choose, and taste a Caribbean that rarely makes it into a glass.
